sources.title: ADXL354/ADXL355 Data Sheet
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rev D; revision history June 2025 (Rev C to Rev D).
sources.locator: PDF pp. 4-6 (ranges); pp. 23-27 (filter defaults, group delay); pp. 28-29 (I2C); pp. 32-33 (synchronization); corresponding manufacturer PDF text at lines 724-730, 914-919, 1023-1028.
sources.observed_operation: Direct manufacturer datasheet review confirmed ADXL355 selectable ±2/±4/±8 g ranges; configurable power-up HPF off, LPF 1000 Hz and ODR 4000 Hz; 0.63 ms digital filter group delay at programmed 4 kHz ODR; and external synchronization timing semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filter and ODR values are power-up defaults and configurable. The datasheet recommends a maximum 800 Hz ODR at 400 kHz I2C; higher ODR can cause missed samples or added noise. Synchronization modes differ in delay and sample-time meaning.
sources.applicability: Concrete ADXL355 example for acquisition audit and a possible reference only. It neither identifies nor specifies the cart logger.
sources.reviser_recheck: Direct manufacturer PDF opened and relevant sections reviewed.

sources.title: Measuring Vibration with Accelerometers
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current HTML; no dated release or commit displayed.
sources.locator: Choosing the Right Accelerometer; Number of Axes; Weight; Mounting Options; Signal Conditioning.
sources.observed_operation: Vendor guide reviewed for mount compliance, added mass, triaxial sensing, range/sensitivity, IEPE conditioning, and calibration considerations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Numeric mount-frequency illustrations are for a typical 100 mV/g accelerometer; they are not universal. Looser attachment reduces usable frequency, and added mounting mass can lower resonance.
sources.applicability: General measurement-design guidance for a future reference and bracket comparison; confirm limits for the selected sensor/structure.
sources.reviser_recheck: Direct NI page opened and mount, mass and conditioning passages reviewed.

sources.title: EVAL-ADXL355Z Linux command line for setting the sample frequency
sources.released_version_or_commit: Q&A opened 2023-04-12; verified vendor response 2023-05-15; EVAL-ADXL355Z, PetaLinux 2022.2/Linux 5.15.36, IIO over SPI at 6.25 MHz.
sources.locator: User setup/report around lines 278-328; vendor support response and interrupt counts around lines 346-395.
sources.observed_operation: The user reported 4 kHz configured and about 2 kHz effective output. Vendor support described missed data-ready interrupts reproduced on a Raspberry Pi path and suggested reading the hardware FIFO on FIFO-full.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A specific non-real-time Linux interrupt path and implementation. FIFO handling was proposed for future work; the thread does not confirm a shipped fix.
sources.applicability: Bounded implementation failure mode motivating effective-rate/loss checks; not evidence of a general sensor defect or cart behavior.
sources.reviser_recheck: Direct original user and vendor posts reviewed; the page's generated summary was not used as sole evidence.

sources.title: Simultaneous Measurements of the Vehicle, Track, and Soil Vibrations at a Surface, Bridge, and Tunnel Railway Line
sources.released_version_or_commit: 2017 version of record; DOI 10.1155/2017/1959286; underlying field campaign in 1994.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 4-5; measurement equipment, procedures, and speed comparisons.
sources.observed_operation: Primary field report describes vehicle accelerometers, track/soil geophones, multiple measurement positions, several track structures, and speed-varying train passages. The 72-channel 2 kHz system is specified for the surface-line section; smaller systems served other sections and the vehicle.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Passenger train and specified railway structures; the measuring car used a 100 kN axle load and 1500 kg wheelset mass. Sampling-rate details differ by section.
sources.applicability: Supports synchronized multi-location references and speed comparison as methods; no cart threshold, amplitude, diagnosis, or safety transfer.
sources.reviser_recheck: Direct Wiley version-of-record page opened; measurement-rate and speed-dependent response passages reviewed.

sources.title: Assessment of integration method for displacement determination using field accelerometer and geophone data
sources.released_version_or_commit: 2017 version of record; Journal of Zhejiang University Science A 18(7), 553-566; DOI 10.1631/jzus.A1600212.
sources.locator: Abstract; field-study methods/results and conclusions, pp. 553-566.
sources.observed_operation: The supplied investigator and critic source maps describe a primary field study comparing accelerometer/geophone-derived displacement with a sleeper LVDT and discussing filtering, speed, load, repeatability, and validity.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific conventional railway track-bed displacement method, sensor placements, speeds, axle loads, and filtering assumptions; its numerical validity conditions are not transferable.
sources.applicability: Method precedent for independent reference instruments and explicit operating validity only; does not validate cart vibration or diagnosis.
sources.reviser_recheck: Attempted both official journal landing and full-text URLs at the stated reviser access time; both returned an internal error. No new direct extraction or numerical claim was made in this stage.
